newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican Cetes rate reverses decline on speculation.
newsitem.headline: Mexican Cetes rate reverses decline on speculation.

text.p: Overnight Cetes rates reversed their initial fall to close 65 basis points higher at 23.80 percent, which traders put down to a technical rebound and some speculative trades.

"Some traders said that they're trying to push rates up a bit so that primary rates won't fall so much, but you also have to take into account that secondary rates had already fallen too far and a slight adjustment was needed," a trader said.
Brokers said that the late rise in rates took place at thin trading volume as most dealers were waiting to see what happens in Tuesday's primary auction.

Overnight Cetes rates opened at 23 percent, which some economists attributed to anticaption that inflation for August would come in near the 1.3 percent figure predicted by the government. (The figure was 1.33 percent.)
Government paper was trading at rates more than 100 basis points below primary levels in the term market in expectation of falls at Tuesday's primary auction.
Benchmark 28-day Cetes were assigned at 25.47 percent in last week's primary auction.
Banco de Mexico offset liquidity shortages in the secondary market earlier by auctioning four credits for a total of 4.904 billion pesos at assignment rates between 25.63 percent and 24.80 percent.
Overnight rates on bank paper closed 35 basis points down from Friday's close at 25.25 percent.
Liquidity shortages on Tuesday will be fueled by 5.968 billion pesos in credits falling due.
